sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. & M. A. Bryan. 1966. Linguistic Analyses: The Non-Bantu Languages of North-Eastern Africa. London: OUP for IAI. Ch. 30 Nilotic, pp. 402-442 (sec. 2b 'Stress').
sources.access_detail: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Gives a group-level 'Stress' paragraph for each unit; the Nilotic/N. Lwo statement (based on Shilluk) would be the only older published generalisation covering the Thuri cluster.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2010. Morphosyntax of Luwo. In O. Hieda (ed.), Descriptive Studies of Nilotic Morphosyntax (Studies in Nilotic Linguistics 2), 1-27. Tokyo: ILCAA; and Storch, Anne. 2007. Grammatical change and emblematic features in Western Nilotic. ACAL 37 proceedings, 1-15.
sources.note: Thuri mentioned only in classification/contact remarks; Storch 2010 p. 26 lists Thuri among languages that 'still remain largely unexplored'. No Thuri stress statement.

sources.citation: Gilley, Leoma G. 2004. The Lwoian family. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 165-174. Entebbe: SIL-Sudan.
sources.note: Nothing for Thuri. p. 165: 'Thuri is very similar to Luwo, and for the most part, they are able to use the Luwo materials. They have not developed a separate writing system at this point.' Stress remarks in the volume concern Shilluk/Dinka/Nuer orthography only; back matter (contents of OPSL 1-8) lists no Thuri paper.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2003. Dynamics of interacting populations: language contact in the Lwoo languages of Bahr el-Ghazal. Studies in African Linguistics 32(1): 65-93.
sources.note: Thuri number-marking data and a note on its two mutually exclusive ATR vowel sets; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2014. A Grammar of Luwo: An Anthropological Approach (Culture and Language Use 12). Amsterdam: Benjamins. Ch. 2 Phonology pp. 19-34.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Nearest sister language (Thuri speakers use Luwo materials per Gilley 2004); its stress/tone section is the best proxy and may comment on Thuri.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2005. The Noun Morphology of Western Nilotic (Nilo-Saharan 21). Koeln: Ruediger Koeppe. Sec. 4.1.3.1 Northern Lwoo vowels pp. 68-73, sec. 4.3 'Tone and Stress' pp. 93-96, sec. 5.4.3.2 'Thuri' pp. 296-302.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, HathiTrust search-only; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.N5 S76 2005)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8026.N5 S76 2005
sources.note: Only modern first-hand source with Thuri field data (Storch's own 2000 fieldwork); sec. 4.3 'Tone and Stress' is the one place a Thuri (or Northern Lwoo incl. Thuri) stress statement is likely to exist. TOC confirmed from DNB scan.
